entities.summary:
Bachelor of Arts is a foundational academic degree that emerged during the Classical era of empires and foundational civilizations, marking a significant shift in the pursuit of knowledge and intellectual inquiry. 

 This degree was first introduced in ancient Greece and Rome, where it was reserved for the elite and served as a stepping stone to higher office and influence. 

 As the Roman Empire expanded, the Bachelor of Arts degree spread throughout the Mediterranean world, becoming a crucial component of the imperial educational system. 

 The legacy of the Bachelor of Arts degree can be seen in the development of medieval universities, such as the University of Bologna and the University of Paris, which built upon the Classical model to create a more comprehensive system of higher education. 

 The impact of this degree has been felt for centuries, shaping the way people think, learn, and engage with the world around them. 

 As the modern university system continues to evolve, the roots of the Bachelor of Arts degree remain a vital part of our intellectual heritage.
